episodes.176904: An extended period of heavy rain, falling at a rate of one to two inches per hour, generated flash flooding that forced road closures for portions of Kauai.
episodes.176949: Moist and unstable air generated some thunderstorms across the Hawaiian Islands.
episodes.177704: A major Arctic cold front blasted through southern New England on the morning of March 3rd. It was followed by a few rounds of strong and locally damaging wind gusts. Temperatures plunged to 10 to 20 below zero on the morning of March 4th. The -10F reading at Boston's Logan Airport was the coldest there since 1957.  Heavy freezing spray occurred, along with Arctic sea smoke.  Wind chill indices reached 30 to 40 below zero across southern New England.

events.narrative: A mesonet station at West Island recorded a gust to 59 mph at 7 PM EST.
A Weatherflow mesonet station at Halfway Rock/Prudence Island recorded a wind gust to 60 mph at 707 PM EST.
A mesonet site at Borden Flats Light recorded a gust to 65 mph at 742 PM EST.
A mesonet site at Woods Hole recorded a gust to 60 mph at 745 PM EST.
A mesonet site at Conimicut Light recorded a gust to 59 mph at 748 PM EST.
Kuhio Highway was closed at the Hanalei Bridge around 8:10am due to water across the road. Later that morning Hauaala Road was closed at the Keapana Bridge due to flooding in Kapaa Stream.
Broadcast media relayed a report that a lightning strike in the Ewa Beach area split a tree. No other damage was reported from this event.
